answer: Each key registers an escrowed identity: a hash of one verified legal person, encrypted to 7 bonded trustees, 5-of-7 to open. Nothing is public. If a jury finds two keys acting in concert, trustees decrypt both and every key sharing that person merges into one seat and forfeits vesting. 100 aliases need 100 real or synthetic IDs (~$30k), and one conviction unmasks all. The fable of a hidden farm fails: no clone is an island. Trustees rotate by VRF and each decrypt is logged on-chain, so none can fish the ocean of keys without a verdict.
